name: Matronae

usually shown as three seated figures of maiden, mother, and crone

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Matronae is the Latin name given to the Deae Matres, the Divine Mothers of the Continental Celts. Monaghan directs the reader to the fuller Deae Matres entry. These mother goddesses were among the most common goddess images found in Celtic lands. They usually appeared as three seated figures, a maiden, a fertile mother, and an aging crone. The goddesses held sacred objects such as a sacrificial knife, an offering plate, and food. They were goddesses of abundance and of the fertility of the land.
objective: Document Matronae, the Latin name of the Deae Matres of the Continental Celts.
key_results: Record Matronae as the name of the Deae Matres.
Record the usual three figures of maiden, mother, and crone.
Record the sacred objects and the role as goddesses of abundance.
